report:
## Verdict: REJECT (5 substantive checklist FAILs on code introduced by this PR, 1 Important unhandled-exception finding, and a diff-added docstring that is false)

## Issue Compliance
Reviewed against issue #318 (SQLite absolute paths / shared URL helper). Criteria came from the workpad; scope is unchanged. Criteria came from the `/prflow:implement` workpad comment: this run's authoritative set, possibly narrowed from the issue. The workpad's criteria and the issue body's do not diverge. The functional criteria (VC-19 to VC-31) all PASS. The docs, mcpb and changelog.d criteria (VC-32 to VC-37) are deferred to the implement orchestrator's Phase 4.1 docs phase, so they were not re-verified and are left out of this verdict. VC-38 (ruff/pytest) is INCONCLUSIVE because the review rule forbids running the suite; the orchestrator settles it in-env.

## Verification Checklist Results
33 passed, 13 failed, 2 inconclusive. 0 by lite probe, 37 by agent (fresh), 4 reused from iter-1, 7 deferred or carried. Normalized (wording-only): 0; ineligible-on-field-defect FAILs: 0.
- VC-9: FAIL. `_probe_sqlite` catches only `sqlite3.Error` around `connect_sqlite`. A non-sqlite3 exception from `sqlite3.connect` escapes unstructured, for example a `ValueError` on an embedded NUL from `sqlite:///a%00b.db` with `read_only=false`. cli.serve catches only `PreflightError`. [src/sqllens/preflight.py:61-82]
- VC-45: FAIL. The `_probe_sqlite` docstring says the message "never [uses] str(exc)", but the ValueError branch raises `PreflightError("database", str(exc))` and embeds SQLAlchemy's parse text. [src/sqllens/preflight.py:56-64]
- VC-46: FAIL. The docstrings say a read-only probe fails on a "non-database file". A zero-byte file opens as an empty DB, `PRAGMA schema_version` returns 0, and the probe passes. [src/sqllens/preflight.py:56, 90-91]
- VC-43: FAIL. `sqlite://:memory:?x=1` reaches make_url and surfaces as "could not parse ... invalid literal for int()" rather than a clear message. No test covers these variants. [src/sqllens/agent/integrations/sqlite/sql_runner.py:49-54]
- VC-44: FAIL. The new OSError branch ("working directory unavailable") has no test. [tests/unit/test_sqlite_url.py; src/sqllens/preflight.py:74-77]
- VC-2: FAIL, claim wording only. make_url raises ValueError (not ArgumentError) for `sqlite://:memory:`. The code catches both, so it is correct. [sql_runner.py:45-54]
- VC-6: FAIL, claim wording only. The drive regex now needs a separator, so `C:foo.db` takes the generic branch. The code is fine. [sql_runner.py:31]
- VC-41: INCONCLUSIVE. Whether Windows SQLite treats `%5C` from `C:\x.db` as a separator cannot be settled without running anything on Windows. [sql_runner.py:76]
- VC-38: INCONCLUSIVE. ruff/pytest were not run, per the review rule.
- VC-32 to VC-37: FAIL (carried), DEFERRED to implement Phase 4.1 (docs, mcpb, changelog.d). Excluded from this verdict per the caller.

<details><summary>Passed items (33 of 48)</summary>

- VC-1, 3, 4, 5, 7, 8 (reused), 10-17, 18 (reused), 19-27, 28-29 (reused), 30, 31, 39, 40, 42, 47, 48

</details>

Coverage shortfall: none (dropped_count 0).

## Code Review Findings
### 🟠 Important / Major
1. A percent-encoded NUL in a SQLite URL (`sqlite:///a%00b.db`) decodes to `a\x00b.db`. With `read_only=false`, `sqlite3.connect` raises `ValueError: embedded null byte`. That error escapes `_probe_sqlite`, whose `except` covers only `sqlite3.Error`, and crashes `serve` with a traceback. The same `ValueError` reaches the runner at query time. Fix: reject a NUL in `sqlite_path_from_url`, or widen the handler. (raised by 1/3 agents; corroborated by checklist VC-9 FAIL) [suspected over-grade: shape 3 — single-source silent-failure-hunter; observable fail-direction is an unstructured crash on a contrived input, but checklist VC-9 FAIL covers it, so it does not match shape 3]
### 🟡 Suggestion / Minor
1. `_WINDOWS_DRIVE` applies on every OS. On Linux, `sqlite:///C:/x.db` opens `/C:/x.db` when read-only and `./C:/x.db` when read-write, so the two modes resolve different files. (raised by 1/3 agents; checklist VC-40 PASS confirms the behavior)
2. The `probe_database` Raises section still says the detail is "a sanitized category". The SQLite detail now names the path or the ValueError text. This line was not modified by the diff, so it is pre-existing comment drift, not a carve-out. (raised by 2/3 agents, signatures not mechanically overlapping)
3. The diff removed the note that sqlite3 `timeout` bounds only the lock wait, not the open. The call site now passes `_DB_CONNECT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`, whose name implies a connect bound. (raised by 1/3 agents)

The diff-added `_probe_sqlite` docstring claims checked in VC-45 and VC-46 are false against HEAD. VC-46's subject is the probe's coverage (functional gap, not capped). VC-45 is a docstring read by no tool and shipped to no consumer (inert). They drive REJECT through rule 1 regardless.

intra-diff contradiction scan: no contradiction found.

checklist.claim: sqlalchemy make_url on sqlite:////tmp/x.db returns .database '/tmp/x.db', on sqlite:///rel.db returns 'rel.db', and on sqlite:///C:/x.db returns 'C:/x.db'
checklist.evidence: SQLAlchemy _parse_url regex (.venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/sqlalchemy/engine/url.py:898-945): after 'sqlite://', host/port groups need a non-slash char, so the '/(?P<database>[^\?]*)' group captures everything after the third slash. sqlite:////tmp/x.db -> '/tmp/x.db'; sqlite:///rel.db -> 'rel.db'; sqlite:///C:/x.db -> 'C:/x.db' (ipv4host excludes '/', port needs ':' directly after '//', which is '/'). Database is only unquoted, no other post-processing. Matches usage at sql_runner.py:52-62.

checklist.claim: make_url raises ArgumentError (not another exception) for 'sqlite://:memory:' and malformed URLs; other exception types would escape as non-ValueError and bypass preflight's except ValueError
checklist.evidence: sqlalchemy url.py _parse_rfc1738_args does int(components['port']) (line ~948), so 'sqlite://:memory:' (port 'memory:') raises ValueError, not ArgumentError; ArgumentError only comes from a regex non-match (e.g. 'nonsense'). ArgumentError is a SQLAlchemyError, not a ValueError. Executing make_url confirmed: 'sqlite://:memory:' -> ValueError; 'sqlite://[::1' -> ValueError; 'nonsense' -> ArgumentError. sql_runner.py:49-50 short-circuits ':memory:' before make_url and :53 catches (ArgumentError, ValueError) and re-raises ValueError, so preflight's except ValueError is safe, but the claim's 'not another exception' wording is wrong.

checklist.claim: Docstring asserts sqlite://, sqlite:///, sqlite://:memory: and sqlite:///:memory: are all in-memory
checklist.evidence: sql_runner.py:34-62 sqlite_path_from_url: sqlite://:memory: returns :memory: via special case (L49-50); sqlite:///:memory: yields database=:memory:; sqlite:// and sqlite:/// yield empty/None database so `or ":memory:"` (L62) returns :memory:. All four forms map to in-memory, matching docstring L38-39.

checklist.claim: parsed.host check rejects sqlite://foo.db but host-free forms (e.g. sqlite://user@/x.db, password, port) are not silently accepted; and parsed.query is the only query carrier
checklist.evidence: sql_runner.py:55-61 rejects parsed.query and any of parsed.host/username/password/port. sqlite://foo.db parses with host=foo.db (SQLAlchemy _parse_url regex, url.py:898-917) so it is rejected; user@, :pw@ and :1 forms are rejected via username/password/port. tests/unit/test_sqlite_url.py:77-84 cover these. SQLAlchemy's only query carrier is the parsed query dict (regex group query, url.py:914,923-936). Minor caveat: blank-valued query text (e.g. '?a=' or bare '?') yields an empty dict because keep_blank_values=False, so is accepted, and empty-string username is falsy; neither affects the path.

checklist.claim: sqlite3 accepts file:///C:/x.db?mode=ro and file:////tmp/x.db?mode=ro (empty authority) without 'invalid uri authority'
checklist.evidence: _readonly_uri (sql_runner.py:65-82) emits file:///C:/x.db?mode=ro for drive paths and file:// + '//tmp/x.db' = file:////tmp/x.db?mode=ro for // paths. SQLite's URI parser (sqlite3ParseUri) skips 'file://' and treats the authority as the text up to the next '/'; an empty authority is accepted (only non-empty, non-'localhost' authorities yield 'invalid uri authority'). Both forms have an empty authority, and the SQLite URI docs list file:///... as valid. Based on documented/known SQLite C behavior; the C source is not in the repo and nothing was run.

checklist.claim: Relative path whose first segment contains ':' (e.g. 'a:b.db') or a drive-like relative name is handled correctly by _readonly_uri; Windows drive regex matches 'C:' without slash too
checklist.evidence: sql_runner.py:31 defines _WINDOWS_DRIVE = re.compile(r"^[A-Za-z]:[\\/]"), which requires a slash or backslash after the colon. It does NOT match 'C:' without a slash (e.g. 'C:foo.db'), so the second half of the claim is false. The first half holds: 'a:b.db' does not match the regex and goes through the generic branch (lines 79-82). quote(..., safe='/') percent-encodes ':' to %3A, giving file:a%3Ab.db?mode=ro, which SQLite decodes. A drive-relative name like 'C:foo.db' takes the same non-drive path.

checklist.claim: The _readonly_uri docstring says the URI never carries a host part, for every input path
checklist.source_excerpt:
The URI never carries a host part, which SQLite rejects with ``invalid uri
    authority``
checklist.evidence: sql_runner.py:65-82 _readonly_uri: Windows drive paths (regex ^[A-Za-z]:[\\/], line 31) become file:///C:...; paths starting '//' (UNC-like, '///x.db') get file:// + path, i.e. an explicit empty authority (file:////host/share, file://///x.db); all other paths become file:<quoted path> with no '//' authority at all; backslash UNC '\\host' is percent-encoded (quote) into the path. quote() encodes ':' and '?' '#', so no input can introduce a host part.

checklist.claim: _WINDOWS_DRIVE matches regardless of OS, so on POSIX a relative path 'C:/x.db' becomes file:///C:/x.db pointing at /C:/x.db rather than the relative file
checklist.evidence: sql_runner.py:31 defines _WINDOWS_DRIVE = re.compile(r'^[A-Za-z]:[\\/]') with no os.name/sys.platform check; _readonly_uri (lines 76-78) applies it unconditionally, so 'C:/x.db' yields 'file:///C:/x.db?mode=ro'. On POSIX that URI path is /C:/x.db, not the relative file 'C:/x.db'.

checklist.claim: A Windows backslash path 'C:\x.db' matches the drive regex but quote(safe='/') encodes the backslash as %5C, which SQLite on Windows may not treat as a separator
checklist.evidence: Mechanics confirmed in src/sqllens/agent/integrations/sqlite/sql_runner.py: _WINDOWS_DRIVE = r'^[A-Za-z]:[\\/]' (line 31) matches 'C:\x.db' (accepts backslash); _readonly_uri (lines 76-78) does database_path[:2] + quote(database_path[2:], safe='/'), so the backslash becomes %5C and the URI is file:///C:%5Cx.db?mode=ro. The consequence ('SQLite on Windows may not treat it as a separator') is a hedged claim about Windows SQLite runtime behavior that cannot be settled from the repo source. SQLite percent-decodes URI paths before use, so the filename should decode back to 'C:\x.db', which Windows accepts, but I could not verify this on Windows, and I ran no tests. Command not run: any Windows SQLite connection or the test suite.

checklist.claim: Percent-encoded characters in the URL path (e.g. sqlite:////tmp/a%20b.db) are handled consistently with how SQLAlchemy's pysqlite dialect would resolve them
checklist.evidence: sqlite_path_from_url (sql_runner.py:34-63) parses via sqlalchemy make_url and returns parsed.database. SQLAlchemy url.py:938-940 unquotes the database component, so sqlite:////tmp/a%20b.db yields /tmp/a b.db, the same as the pysqlite dialect. _readonly_uri then re-encodes with quote(safe='/') for the SQLite file: URI (test_safety.py:677-679). factory.py:228 and preflight.py:62 both use the helper.

checklist.source_excerpt:
The message names the path

checklist.evidence: preflight.py:61-64: the ValueError branch does `raise PreflightError("database", str(exc))`, so the docstring's 'never str(exc)' (lines 56-57) is false for that raise site. sqlite_path_from_url (sql_runner.py:51-61) raises ValueError at line 54 with `{exc}` of the sqlalchemy make_url error embedded, and at 56/58 with fixed text. The sqlite3.Error branch (lines 71-82) does avoid str(exc). Absolute claim is partially wrong.

checklist.claim: The docstrings' claim that a read-only probe fails on a non-database file (as well as a directory) via PRAGMA schema_version holds, including for a zero-byte file
checklist.source_excerpt: so a directory or non-database file fails here
checklist.evidence: preflight.py:69-70 only runs conn.execute('PRAGMA schema_version').fetchone() under mode=ro and catches sqlite3.Error (71). SQLite treats a zero-byte file as a valid empty database: PRAGMA schema_version returns 0 and raises nothing, so the probe passes. A garbage non-database file or a directory does raise (file is not a database / unable to open), so the docstrings at preflight.py:56 and 90-91 are right for those but overstate it for a zero-byte file. No code in the probe checks file size. This is from SQLite semantics and the code; nothing was run.

checklist.claim: A sqlite3.OperationalError from a read-only open of a missing file at query time (SqliteRunner) reaches MCP clients / verify-memory as a structured isError result, not an unguarded crash
checklist.evidence: SqliteRunner._run_sql_blocking (sql_runner.py) calls connect_sqlite(read_only=True) which raises sqlite3.OperationalError for a missing file via mode=ro. It runs inside run_blocking_sql, called from RunSqlTool.execute, whose `except Exception` (agent/tools/run_sql.py:190-202) converts it to ToolResult(success=False) with an error notification. Any exception escaping send_message is caught by query_database_impl_with_widgets (tools/query_database.py ~'except Exception' after UnsafeSqlError/RlsError) and re-raised as RuntimeError(_INTERNAL_ERROR_MESSAGE). A failed tool result becomes is_error and AgentRunError, which server.py maps to isError. verify-memory calls the same function.
